cards.front: Which cranial nerve supplies the tongue muscles except palatoglossus? [___]
cards.context: CN XII supplies intrinsic and most extrinsic tongue muscles. Palatoglossus instead receives vagal supply; a lower motor XII lesion makes the protruded tongue deviate toward the weak side.

cards.front: The cranial nerve carrying carotid sinus sensory information is [___].
cards.context: The carotid sinus senses arterial stretch and sends blood-pressure information through cranial nerve IX. Oxygen and carbon-dioxide chemistry is sensed by the nearby carotid body, not the sinus.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: The rotator-cuff muscle classically associated with initiating shoulder abduction is [___].
cards.context: Supraspinatus contributes to initial shoulder abduction and helps stabilise the humeral head with the other rotator-cuff muscles.

cards.front: Which cranial nerve carries taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue? [___]
cards.context: Taste travels from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue through the chorda tympani to the facial nerve. Proximal facial-nerve injury can impair both taste and facial movement.

cards.front: The cranial nerve providing parasympathetic supply to the heart, lungs, foregut and midgut is [___].
cards.context: This links autonomic control in the chest with digestion. Hindgut parasympathetic supply instead comes from pelvic splanchnic nerves.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: The cranial nerve carrying vestibular information from the inner ear is [___].
cards.context: Vestibular input helps stabilise gaze and posture. This explains vertigo or imbalance after vestibular pathway injury.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: The main muscle extending the elbow is the [___].
cards.context: Its tendon inserts on the olecranon, behind the elbow axis. Contraction pulls the forearm into extension.

cards.front: A complete right sixth-nerve palsy causes horizontal diplopia that is worse on right gaze because the right eye cannot [___].
cards.context: Weakness of the affected lateral rectus produces horizontal binocular diplopia and an inward deviation of that eye. The diplopia is worse when the patient looks towards the weak muscle.

cards.front: Which movement is produced primarily by the medial rectus? [___]
cards.context: The medial rectus is the horizontal muscle that moves the eye towards the nose. It is supplied by the inferior division of cranial nerve III.
